requirements.requirement: Create a local certificate authority named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1
requirements.summary: openssl generated a self-signed CA key/cert with subject=issuer=CN=OS Comparison Root CA, CA:TRUE, 4096-bit RSA, SHA256, 10-year validity, directly verified via `openssl x509 -subject -issuer -dates`.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA certificate as a trusted system certificate authority
requirements.summary: Certificate copied to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/, update-ca-trust extract run; `trust list` shows label 'OS Comparison Root CA' with trust: anchor; `openssl verify` against the system ca-bundle returns OK, confirming system-wide trust.

requirements.requirement: Trusted CA state remains valid/recoverable across a restart (cross-checked via mandatory restart protocol, not itself part of the public contract but relevant to durability)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 98aa35f5... captured with CA healthy; reboot issued and acknowledged; polling showed connection timeouts then recovery with new boot_id 69b4ee23...; post-restart verification shows anchor file present, trust list still shows anchor, openssl verify OK, and systemctl is-system-running reports 'running'. This directly demonstrates the full disruption-and-recovery transition.

overall_summary: The executor created a 4096-bit self-signed Root CA named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1, installed it into the system trust anchors, and directly verified via `trust list` and `openssl verify` that it is trusted. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also completed with direct, coherent evidence: a healthy pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged reboot, a bounded disruption (connection timeouts), a changed boot_id confirming the restart, and post-restart re-verification showing the CA anchor and openssl verify still pass with the system fully running. No unnecessary mutations or residue beyond expected reboot artifacts were observed.
limitations: Evidence relies on a single executor attempt with no independent re-verification outside the captured commands.
The private key location (/root/os-comparison-ca/ca.key) and its permissions were not explicitly checked for security hardening, though this was not a stated task requirement.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor commands map cleanly to task purposes: OS/sudo discovery (read-only), boot_id baseline capture (prerequisite for restart protocol), CA creation/installation/verification (core task), a single safe backgrounded reboot with polling (mandatory restart protocol), and post-restart re-verification. No unnecessary or unrelated mutations were found. The only residue is a small /tmp/reboot.log left from the backgrounded reboot command and new systemd-private tmp dirs created automatically by the fresh boot's own services — both are expected, bounded, low-risk side effects of a sanctioned reboot rather than executor-created clutter, and package-health and failed-services checks show no damage post-restart.
